subject: Trial onboarding: success criteria, dual eval path, timeline & owners
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medisys.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@medisys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Trial onboarding: success criteria, dual eval path, timeline & owners

Hi Sofia / Tom —

Great conversation this morning. Quick recap and a concrete proposal for the POC so we can get to an operational trial next week. I kept this intentionally short and action-oriented.

Why two evaluation paths? From our call it sounded like you want both a fast offline signal to narrow model/config choices and a short live shadow to validate end-to-end behavior with real traffic. The dual-path reduces risk while keeping the timeline tight.

Proposal (high level):
- Duration: 3 weeks total (1 week offline + 2 weeks live shadow)
- Offline: we run a curated holdout evaluation on your sample records (anonymized subset). Goal is to select top 2 model/config candidates. Deliverable: ranked results + confusion examples. Owner: Marissa.
- Live shadow: route ~10% of traffic to Redwood shadow for 2 weeks (read-only). Monitor accuracy, hallucination rate, latency, and downstream metric lift where available. Owner: Vivek (ops) + Lauren (SRE/pipeline).

Success criteria (pass/fail gates):
1) Accuracy: model A or B >= 88% on offline labeled set AND no more than 2% regression vs baseline on key intent classes in shadow.
2) Safety: zero high-severity hallucinations on a daily sample review; <= 0.5% flagged safety incidents overall.
3) Latency: median inference p95 <= 400ms in shadow.
4) Cost: estimated per-1k-token cost <= X (we'll share numbers after offline run).

Evaluation rubric (attached): accuracy, recall on priority intents, false positive rate for sensitive intents, safety flags, latency, and token cost. Each category scored 0-5; pass if weighted score >= 18/25. Marissa attached the first draft rubric and sample scoring sheet.

Next steps / asks from MediSys:
- Sofia: confirm you can share the sample CSV (anonymized) by EOD Tuesday (we received a partial export earlier).
- Tom: confirm which intents are must-pass (e.g., "prior auth", "rx change", "clinical escalation") so we can weight the rubric.
- MediSys IT: allow outbound flow from your test tenant to our shadow endpoint (I will send a short network checklist).

Internal owners:
- Marissa: offline eval, rubric execution, result pack
- Vivek: shadow setup, routing, runbooks, dashboarding
- Lauren: infra/SRE support, latency SLO monitoring

I attached: trial-schedule-and-checkpoints.pdf, dual_eval_rubric_v1.xlsx, and a small sample manifest for the anonymized CSV.

I'll stand up the workspace once Sofia confirms sample availability. Happy to jump on a short 30-min alignment tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks,
Vivek

--

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear plan. Quick answers:
- We can deliver the anonymized sample CSV by Tuesday EOD. I will have IT scrub direct identifiers first. File will be ~3k rows.
- Must-pass intents: prior auth, clinical escalation, and "adverse event" tagging — those three need to be weighted heavier.
- Shadow routing: Ops can open for outbound to your test endpoint; I expect network contact (IT) will be on the thread tomorrow.

We like the dual-path approach. One ask: can the offline run include an explicit calibration step so the team can see how prompt templates affect precision/recall? If so, please call out who will own prompt variants.

Subject: Re: Trial onboarding: success criteria, dual eval path, timeline & owners

Thanks Tom — yes, we can include prompt calibration. Short follow-up with more detail on the offline plan and the rubric flow (see attached xlsx). Key points:

Offline plan (week 1):
- Data: run against your 3k anonymized rows + a holdout labeled set of ~500 rows you confirm as ground truth.
- Variants: we will evaluate up to 4 prompt/template + temperature combinations per model candidate (two model sizes, two quantization configs).
- Outputs: per-variant confusion matrices, per-intent precision/recall, a set of counterexamples tagged for safety review.

Rubric highlights: (weights in parentheses)
- Priority intent recall (40%) — we will weight "prior auth", "clinical escalation", and "adverse event" highest as requested.
- Safety flags (20%) — manual review for hallucinations and PHI disclosure risk.
- Latency (15%) — median and p95 measured on a Redwood-stubbed infra profile.
- Cost estimate (10%) — tokenized cost per 1k infer requests at observed batch sizes.
- Operability / integration risk (15%) — simple checklist (data mapping, dev time, monitoring).

Pass criteria: weighted score >= 72% AND no safety block triggered on any high-severity example. If both top variants fail, we will recommend configuration changes and re-run a targeted offline pass (additional 3 days).

Ownership notes: I will run the offline experiments and produce the scorecard by Friday of week 1. Vivek / Lauren will own the shadow rollout and daily dashboard during weeks 2–3.

Attachments referenced: dual_eval_rubric_v1.xlsx (scoring sheet), trial-schedule-and-checkpoints.pdf, medisys_sample_pii_subset.csv (manifest only).

I'll also add a short checklist for your IT in the Drive folder (link below).

- Marissa
